usage and declared editable settings,
**And** net daily hours are the standard input with coherent detailed timetable/break
settings under Advanced. Existing assignment/override references remain explicit.

**Given** proposed calculation-relevant changes and effective date/reason,
**When** I proceed to review,
**Then** I see old/new settings, applicability, affected employees and the changed inherited
values, with unchanged overridden values separately identified,
**And** direct/default-dependent usage is assessed under current allowed scope. Review
also lists existing requests needing attention where applicable; missing required impact
verification is not a zero-impact result or permission to publish blindly.

**Given** an 18-person profile changes Friday from eight to seven net working hours,
**When** 17 employees inherit Friday and Ana has a six-hour override,
**Then** review shows the 17 inherited changes and Ana's retained six hours,
**And** this example is illustrative, not an imposed working week, country default or

**When** Leave publishes the change,
**Then** it retains the profile identity and creates one new immutable effective schedule
version with required attribution/reason/audit and compact operation outcome,
**And** old applicable settings/version references and submitted calculation snapshots
remain meaningful. No overlapping applicable versions or silent historical overwrite;
unchanged saves/replay do not create fictitious calculation versions/change events.

**Given** a future applicability boundary,
**When** current and future-date consumers resolve schedules,
**Then** each uses the profile settings applicable to its requested employee-local date,
**And** the future schedule does not become current early. Work-timezone transition,
DST, advanced/net and partial-holiday semantics follow the completed typed domain contract;

**Given** employee overrides, explicit assignments and organization-default dependencies,

nonoverridden settings follow that profile's applicable version,
**And** this action does not choose another organization default/profile or alter People
location/employment/membership. Incompatible overrides require explicit resolution under
current-impact validation; never silently discard them to make the shared edit succeed.

**Given** prior submitted requests or entitlement effects,

**Then** prior recorded calculations/dates/decisions remain unchanged and required attention
follows existing explicit correction/renewed-acknowledgement rules,

impact/reference waits are outside short locks; no timestamp-only concurrency or typing-
time published configuration. Actor fields are server-derived.

### Story 2.24: Archive an unused work profile without losing its history

**Scope approved with Active/Inactive/Deactivate presentation, 2026-10-12; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave work-
profile lifecycle API/UI. Consumes completed 2.19–2.23 profile/assignment/default/version
and current-authority foundations. No later report, approval or archive-management engine.

As a Leave administrator authorized to manage schedules,
I want to archive a profile once it is no longer needed for current or planned work,
So that it disappears from new choices while earlier arrangements and recorded leave
remain understandable.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a permitted saved profile,
**When** I open Archive,
**Then** its current/scheduled assignment and organization-default dependencies are checked,
**And** the action is blocked while any current/planned arrangement depends on it or it
is the applicable default. Historical references alone do not require erasing the past
or automatically rewriting employee settings. Exact dependency predicate is a pre-story input.

**Given** assignment/default dependencies block archive,
**When** I inspect why,
**Then** authorized blocking employee/default references link to completed assignment/
default settings with shared return-to-origin/focus behavior,
**And** those changes retain their own review/date/reason/override safeguards. On return,
eligibility is refreshed; a stale empty list cannot authorize archive. Do not offer
archive-and-move-everyone or clear settings automatically.

**Given** the profile is no longer required by current/scheduled/default settings,
**When** I explicitly confirm archiving against current reviewed state,
**Then** Leave records the archive marker/actor/time with guarded revision, required change
history and compact operation result atomically,
**And** the profile is unavailable for new ordinary assignments/default choices. Its stable
identity, earlier/future version evidence and request/assignment references are retained.
Use the accepted archive timestamp as simple Active/Archived presentation; no separate
archive database or workflow is needed.

**Given** prior schedule/version references and recorded leave,
**When** an authorized historical view or correction resolves them,
**Then** the archived identity and relevant preserved version remain interpretable,
**And** recorded calculations/decisions are not changed, deleted or reconstructed from a
generic audit log. Historical resolution is distinct from permission to newly select
an archived profile, and never grants business-record access by possessing an ID.

**Given** a concurrent employee assignment, default change or scheduled use after review,
**When** archive and the competing command are confirmed,
**Then** shared local write/constraint guards prevent a newly invalid active reference,
**And** either valid use wins and blocks archive, or archive wins and new use is refused.
Relevant changed state requires renewed review; no optimistic hidden fallback to another
profile. Historical/default/ended-employment edge cases are defined and tested before readiness.

**Given** wrong organization, missing authority, Cancel, outage or response loss,
**When** Archive resolves,
**Then** current authorized original-operation recovery prevents duplicate history and
reports actual committed state, with safe typed error/current-review handling,
**And** required local evidence failure aborts the mutation. External checks remain outside
short locks; browser-supplied actor/status fields cannot archive a record directly.

**Given** initially failing acceptance and actual restricted Leave/current-access fixtures,
**When** delivery records evidence,
**Then** current/scheduled/default blocking, related-setting return, historical retention,
concurrent assignment/archive ordering, safe retry and cross-org/API denial pass,
**And** earlier E1 current-versus-historical reference and draft-preservation rules remain
compatible. Existing version/snapshot tests supplement the UI, not mocked success alone.

**Given** the approved reference-availability terminology and a profile archive marker,
**When** profile availability and its action are presented,
**Then** the user sees Active/Inactive and Deactivate under the accepted 2026-10-12 terminology, while the retained archive timestamp/history and all current/scheduled/default dependency guards remain; older Active/Archived presentation wording is superseded only for these user-facing labels.

0020/0022/0023/0025/0031/0035/0049/0051/0059; Leave ADR-0003/0023/0086 and approved
profile lifecycle/return-navigation UX. Reactivation/purge and employee/offboarding are
outside this item; no hidden removal of employee overrides or organization membership.

### Story 2.25: See actionable setup status from saved configuration

**Scope approved with Leave-specific/derived-status clarification, 2026-10-12; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave setup
assessment API/UI and authorized shared People/Access clients. E2 increment consumes the
completed people/supervisor/work-profile/calendar configuration. The full approved design
has three areas; E3 owns actual leave-type/policy assessment integration when that domain
is delivered. Do not hide a future E3 implementation dependency inside E2 acceptance or
claim full organization readiness before authoritative assessments are implemented.

As an authorized Leave administrator,
I want to see remaining setup issues and navigate to their settings,
So that I can configure the organization in a useful order without manual completion flags.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** current authorized setup-read access in the organization,
**When** I open Setup,
**Then** the approved presentation groups People and supervisors, Work profiles and holidays,
and Leave types and policies with links to available authorized settings,
**And** there is no mandatory sequence, manual Mark complete, separate activation action,
consultant email-approval tracker or standard opening-balances checklist row.

**Given** an implemented authoritative section assessment,
**When** its saved configuration is read,
**Then** status is Not started for missing essentials, Needs review for known invalid/
incomplete settings, Ready when its required checks pass, or Could not check with Retry
when it cannot be assessed,
**And** unknown/unsupported assessment is not Ready/empty/Not started merely from missing
implementation. Actual E2 assessments use real delivered configuration/owner reads;
E3 adds/proves its own policy results rather than E2 faking that domain's validation.

**Given** there are no employees in the organization,
**When** People/setup is assessed,
**Then** People remains Not started and normal configuration tasks are offered,
**And** there are no invented employee names/errors or demands to import opening balances.
A legitimate zero balance or empty holiday year alone is not proof of missing setup.

**Given** employees and delivered required configuration exist,
**When** People/supervisor and work-arrangement assessment runs,
**Then** applicable employment/work-profile/timezone/calendar/reference and supervisor
eligibility issues are listed with permitted employee/setting links,
**And** department/location nulls do not invalidate employment; missing approval route
matters only under the applicable configured Leave policy. Define which current/future/
ended employees/date/context participate before readiness, without guessing UTC today.

**Given** a setup issue is selected,
**When** its linked existing settings form is opened and saved or cancelled,
**Then** shared related-record context/focus/return behavior brings the administrator back
and the affected section re-assesses from saved state,
**And** uncommitted local edits cannot mark a section complete. Refreshing one section does
not erase other authorized results; relevant access loss hides protected details.

**Given** required service/assessment reads fail,
**When** setup loads or refreshes,
**Then** the affected assessment shows Could not check and safe Retry rather than a false
missing employee/location/profile or successful empty state,
**And** current authority and other independent usable configuration sections remain intact.
Results carry declared observation evidence/stale handling; they are not reusable
permission grants or a stored independent ready flag.

**Given** saved configuration changes or a consequential action is attempted,
**When** its own application path validates inputs,
**Then** it enforces current authoritative rules independently of checklist status,
**And** a displayed Ready never authorizes submission or waives readiness/contracts.
Keep lightweight draft preservation separate from business setup and employee admission.
Actual policy/approval/calculation consumers own their full validity checks.

**Given** initially failing acceptance and actual delivered E2 configuration/HTTP fixtures,
**When** the E2 item is verified,
**Then** implemented People/work-arrangement sections prove empty/known issue/ready/outage,
permission-scoped links and save/return/reassessment with no manual status writes,
**And** absent policy assessment cannot produce a false Ready. E3 later proves all policy
predicates and end-to-end three-area results using its own real configuration. Bound/split

## Setup ownership and derived-status clarification — 2026-10-12

User asks whether 2.25 is Leave or cross-app setup, whether status is stored in a record,
and why consequential validation was mentioned. Clarify the current authoritative scope:
this is Leave setup for the selected organization, using Leave-owned configuration plus
People/Access facts needed by Leave. It is not an organization-wide completion process
for every app, public Scribeswell or account-scoped PtS. Recommend the visible title Leave
setup to make that boundary clear. A later platform overview could link to/consume an
explicit app summary but is not silently introduced in this story.

A section status is derived API response data rendered as a badge/row in the UI. Saved
configuration means actual employee/employment references, profile/default assignments,
calendar and policy definitions in their owning stores; it is not one separate setup
record with a manually saved status. Do not persist independent Not started/Ready flags
that drift from those facts. Example: no employees => People Not started; an employee
with neither usable explicit profile nor valid fallback => Needs review; all applicable
implemented checks pass => Ready; a required owner read fails => Couldn't check. Read
results are bounded observations, not a permanent capability or overall BMAD readiness.

Recommend using the existing Leave forms/components inside the Leave setup flow, opening
focused edits in approved drawers or navigating to the existing editor with return context.
Use shared People/access administration controls/contracts where appropriate. Do not copy
forms or import Leave-specific UI into another application's implementation, add iframe/
microfrontend infrastructure or require a global platform setup engine. This keeps the
approved HTTP/runtime and app-silo boundaries while preserving the user's existing views.

The submission/approval sentence explains that a derived setup status is informational:
configuration can change after the page is loaded, so consequential operations read their
current actual inputs under existing rules. It introduces no extra checklist step or new
validation policy. Example: setup was Ready, then a setting changes; the next submission
cannot authorize itself from the earlier badge. Clarification only; 2.25 remains under
discussion and no stored status, API/view implementation or cross-app architecture change.


Leave setup clarification approved — 2026-10-12: 2.25 is Leave setup for the current
organization. Status is derived API response/UI data from actual saved owner facts, not
an independent stored ready field or a cross-app completion record. Existing Leave/shared
forms open through approved drawers/navigation/return context; no duplicate editors or
cross-app view embedding engine. Current action validation remains independent because
configuration may change after an assessment. No implementation/readiness completion.

### Story 2.26: View an employee's employment and Leave work settings together

**Scope approved with Leave entry/navigation clarification, 2026-10-12; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave employee
settings summary/read API/UI with authorized Identity/People/Access HTTP clients. Consumes
completed E2 employment/access/profile/override writers and read contracts. E2 delivers
Employment & approval and Work schedule; E3 adds the approved Leave entitlement section
with its actual policy/balance/override semantics. No future E3/E5 UI prerequisite for the
E2 summary's independent real-data acceptance.

As an authorized Leave administrator,
I want a readable employee summary with clear settings and focused edit entry points,
So that I can understand and maintain their setup without searching across disconnected
screens or duplicating shared employee data.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the exact employee/current organization and permitted section read access,
**When** I open the employee's Leave settings,
**Then** Employment & approval shows permitted shared person/account-link status,
employment periods/status, optional department/location and supervisor/Leave eligibility,
**And** those fields are read through their current owner contracts with correct scope.
Accountless/unassigned is a valid value where specified; person identity is not copied
into a separate Leave employee master or inferred from email matching.

**Given** permitted Work schedule read access,
**When** the summary loads that section,
**Then** I see explicit profile or default source, applicable net working days/hours,
timezone, holiday calendar and standard-day conversion with overrides identified,
**And** net daily hours are the normal summary while detailed timetables are available
where configured. Inherited source and explicit override are distinct, including equal-
valued overrides. No implicit team/location profile merge or arbitrary country defaults.

**Given** an editable section and current matching management authority,
**When** I choose its focused Edit/action,
**Then** the existing approved writer form/drawer opens for the exact employee/organization,
**And** completed saving/review/reason/date/current-impact safeguards apply without another
implementation of the edit. Save/Cancel returns to the summary/focus and refreshes the
actual affected state; unconfirmed edits do not change summary data or readiness.

**Given** read authority without the relevant edit/role/impact authority,
**When** the summary renders,
**Then** permitted information remains readable while mutation actions are unavailable,
**And** role-assignment shortcuts use the shared drawer with their own authority. No
employee-summary permission grants access to medical documents, other employees beyond
scope or a broader role-management function. Later request/balance/history controls stay
with their own authorized consumers.

**Given** a required owner read fails or configuration cannot be interpreted,
**When** the summary is loaded/refreshed,
**Then** affected section status is honest unavailable/Retry or known setup issue, not
empty periods, Unassigned or zero balance substituted for a failure,
**And** other independently authorized results may remain usable only under declared
stale/access rules. The summary-load shape composes owners at the API boundary, without
separate browser business-table access or a distributed snapshot promise.

**Given** relevant employee/account/profile/permission state changes while a form is open,
**When** its read/action is attempted,
**Then** the exact target/current access and owner revision rules are enforced,
**And** a stale summary does not authorize a write or wrong-account navigation. Earlier
recorded work arrangements/employee history remain, with current versus historical date
meaning displayed clearly. No unfinished form survival across browser closure is promised.

**Given** E3 entitlement configuration/read features are later delivered,
**When** their consuming stories extend this summary,
**Then** the approved Leave entitlement group and separate balance actions use real current
policy/override/calculation data and their own permissions,
**And** E2 does not pre-create policy/ledger tables, invent balances or claim those features
are ready. The group/layout remains a traced E3 obligation, not an E2 fake implementation.

**Given** initially failing acceptance and real delivered E2 owner HTTP/persistence fixtures,
**When** this item is verified,
**Then** linked/accountless employees, periods/placement/supervisor status, inherited/overridden
work values, section authority, owner failures and focused edit/return/refreshed state pass,
**And** mobile/keyboard/focus behavior follows approved UX. E3/E5 add their real domain
summary/history tests; a mockup or mocked successful response is not integrated proof.

**Traceability:** Features §2 employee Leave settings groups and source ownership; tracker
Phase 2 settings summary/focused edits and Phase 5 work configuration; spine AD-1/2/4/5/12;
platform ADR-0019/0020/0022/0023/0025/0031/0040/0041/0042/0049/0051/0058/0059;
Leave ADR-0023/0086/0122/0125 and approved Employee Leave settings preview/journey.
Leave entitlement/balance actions/history are E3/E5/E6 consumers; no generic HR dashboard
or duplicated approval/policy engine is introduced.

**Impacts/readiness:** Define exact per-section read/field/edit authority and projected DTOs,
People/Identity/Access target lookup versus `/me` constraints, minimal account/person data,
current/date/version/source fields, bounded composed calls and null/unavailable/stale
contracts before readiness. Match approved writers/return targets and require fresh actual
checks on action. Promote proven read-summary/source/status/section/return patterns only
where domain-neutral; Leave owns its grouped employee composition and no app-specific
cross-silo UI import. Update scaffold config/source/test references when supported, owner
docs/runbook/API types and generated agent usage guidance where needed. Count real cross-
owner integration/UI in sizing; no E2/global coverage or implementation readiness pass.
No employee settings, records, code, schema or deployment changed by planning.

### Story 3.1: Create and view an organization's leave types

**Scope approved by the user, 2026-10-12; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave
API/web/persistence. Consumes E1 Identity/Access, owner-write/recovery/attribution,
type/version/choice contracts and E2 organization configuration entry points.
User approved the clarified draft-selection criterion below, then requested the next story.

As a Leave Manager with current configuration permission,
I want to create and view leave types for my organization,
So that I can establish recognizable categories before configuring their policies.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** current policy-read authority in the selected organization,
**When** I open leave-type configuration,
**Then** I see its types, status and saved metadata, with current policy information
where configured,
**And** missing policy configuration is shown honestly; failed loading is distinguishable
from an empty catalogue. Policy detail read/display is completed by its own consuming
story; this story does not depend on a future policy editor or calculator to work.

**Given** current policy-management authority,
**When** I create a type,
**Then** I can enter its name, code, description, color, icon and permitted request modes,
with Full days, Half day and Hours initially permitted and a way to restrict that selection,
**And** the form uses explicit whole-form Save / Cancel and preserves entered values
after validation failure. Arbitrary day fractions are not offered.

**Given** valid configuration,
**When** I save,
**Then** the server atomically creates one organization-scoped type and its initial
published metadata version, with attribution and required change evidence,
**And** a retry after a lost response creates no duplicate. Publication here concerns
E1's offered type metadata, not activation of an entitlement policy.

**Given** an existing code in this organization, including an archived type's code,
**When** I attempt to reuse it,
**Then** creation fails safely without repurposing the existing identity or losing my input.

**Given** a newly created leave type,
**When** an employee opens or refreshes their draft form,
**Then** they can select that type and save their unfinished input,
**And** selecting it does not bypass the policy and eligibility checks required before
submission. E1's scoped published pointer/modes and safe choice-refresh behavior remain
binding; no entitlement, request-date eligibility or readiness is inferred from selection.

**Given** denied/revoked authority or another organization's identifier,
**When** the API is called directly,
**Then** it prevents unauthorized disclosure or mutation,
**And** unavailable access verification produces retryable failure rather than an empty
catalogue or assumed permission. Recovered operation outcomes also require current access.

**Given** keyboard or mobile use,
**When** I create, save or cancel,
**Then** validation, focus, feedback and changed-form exit behavior follow approved shared UX.

**Traceability / planned verification:** Features Permissions/§4/7; BIZ-05/06 (partial
coverage); Leave ADR-0002/0086/0124; platform operation/revision/attribution/integrity
and saving contracts; [E1 choices](../../apps/leave/docs/architecture/contracts/e1-draft-choice-resolution.md).
Pair API/database scope, retained-code, default/restricted modes, immutable version/pointer,
attribution and duplicate/lost-response checks with browser create/save/cancel and real
draft select/save/reopen coverage. Preserve E1-AC-03/06/13/15/16/17 as applicable.
Exact test paths/commands and source-to-test mapping are delivery inputs; no tests executed.

**Pre-story inputs / sizing:** Bind additional metadata ownership/bounds and migration
compatibility with E1's existing schema, capability/API/error/operation contracts and
restricted runtime writer authority. Do not invent effective-policy selection from the
draft-choice pointer. List/create/read only; policy configuration, reviewed starter policy
activation, used-type edits/deactivation/restoration and employee assignments retain later
owners. Final agent sizing and readiness remain pending.

**Impacts:** Scaffold: prove/reuse generic scoped/versioned creation, attribution and
operation recovery with schema-validated choices and reference tests where applicable;
no generic Leave catalogue engine. Shared UI: reuse collection/form/selector/error and
Save / Cancel patterns; promote only proven domain-neutral additions. Agent context:
existing instructions suffice. Documentation: epics/tracker checkpoint and owning
contract/test mapping updates. ADR: existing accepted decisions suffice; no amendment.

### Story 3.2: View a leave type's policy and version history

**Scope approved by the user, 2026-10-12; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave
API/web/persistence. Consumes Story 3.1's type identity and E1 current-access/read
foundations. Controlled owner fixtures supply the required versioned policy data;
no later editor or calculator is a prerequisite for completing this read story.

As a Leave Manager with current policy-read permission,
I want to see a leave type's current policy, scheduled changes and previous versions,
So that I understand its rules before configuring or changing them.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an authorized manager viewing a leave type,
**When** they open its configuration,
**Then** the current policy appears as a readable summary grouped into Entitlement,
Request rules, Approval, and Documents & privacy,
**And** its effective date is prominent, with advanced details expandable.

**Given** no policy has been configured,
**When** the summary opens,
**Then** it clearly states that policy configuration is missing,
**And** it shows no invented allowance, approval route or Ready status.

**Given** a scheduled future policy version,
**When** the summary opens,
**Then** the current policy remains the main summary, with a Scheduled change notice
showing the effective date and a link to that version,
**And** future settings are not presented as already applicable.

**Given** retained previous versions,
**When** I open policy history and select a version,
**Then** I can read its recorded settings and effective dates,
**And** viewing it changes no configuration or historical request evidence.

**Given** automatic entitlement or manual-only grants,
**When** I read the entitlement summary,
**Then** it explains the configured choice in plain language, distinguishing annual
allowance from current balance and leave-year boundaries from monthly instalments,
**And** illustrative explanations are not presented as legal defaults or calculated
employee balances.

**Given** failed loading, denied access or an organization switch,
**When** policy data is requested,
**Then** loading failure is distinguishable from missing configuration, current
authorization is enforced, and stale responses cannot display another organization's policy.

**Traceability / planned verification:** Features §4; BIZ-05/06 (partial coverage);
Leave ADR-0002/0086 and applicable entitlement-language decisions, especially 0090/0103;
approved Leave EXPERIENCE policy summary/scheduled/history and DESIGN policy groups;
platform loading/disclosure/navigation and current-access rules. Verify version/date
boundaries and API isolation alongside browser navigation, keyboard/mobile disclosure,
missing versus unavailable states and delayed-response organization-switch cases.
Owner fixtures represent current/scheduled/previous versions without a future production
editor. No runtime tests executed; exact test paths/commands and final source mapping pending.

**Pre-story inputs / sizing:** Bind version-selection/effective-date interpretation,
read schema and disclosure rules, immutable version representation and fixture ownership.
Do not select policy via E1's draft-choice pointer or create calculation snapshots on reads.
Fixtures/protocol must cover all display states, including no current policy; no implicit
write, publishing worker, frontend accrual calculation or future-story dependency.
Final agent sizing and readiness remain pending.

**Impacts:** Scaffold: reuse/prove scoped read and retained-version reference patterns
where domain-neutral, with actual reference tests before promotion. Shared UI: reuse
summaries/disclosures, loading/error and contextual navigation; Leave owns policy content.
Agent context: existing instructions suffice. Documentation: owning read/version contracts,
test mapping and epics/tracker checkpoint. ADR: accepted decisions suffice; no amendment.

### Story 3.3: Configure and publish a leave type's first policy

**Delivery split approved — 2026-10-15:** Retain this agreed scope as the traceability
parent and decompose into **3.3-A** (complete authorized initial-policy API/review/
publication with actual persistence acceptance) followed by **3.3-B** (approved four-
section web editor/review/publication integrated with that completed API). No original
acceptance is removed, invalid partial policy activated or required evidence deferred.
Detail the two children collaboratively in that order; split approval is not approval
of unpresented child criteria or a final sizing/readiness PASS. Deliver both before
dependent initial-policy editor consumers such as 3.4; appendix placement does not
change dependency order. Published versions remain immutable; later accepted ADRs and
untracked configuration scope apply where relevant. No application implementation.

**Scope approved by the user, 2026-10-12; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave
API/web/persistence. Consumes Stories 3.1–3.2 and E1/E2 current authority, configuration,
operation recovery and version/read foundations. Initial configuration/publication only;
employee assignment, balance calculations and changes to used policies retain later owners.

As a Leave Manager with current policy-management permission,
I want to configure and review the first policy for an unused leave type,
So that its rules are explicitly agreed before employees use it.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a leave type without a policy,
**When** I open policy configuration,
**Then** a dedicated editor provides four directly accessible sections: Entitlement,
Request rules, Approval, and Documents & privacy,
**And** edits remain uncommitted until explicit publication; leaving changed input follows
the shared discard confirmation. No separate persisted administrative draft system.

**Given** the entitlement section,
**When** I configure its rules,
**Then** I can choose automatic annual entitlement with daily, upfront or monthly
availability, or manual-only grants, and configure the applicable period, proration,
carry-over, cap and expiry settings,
**And** conditional fields and plain-language explanations follow the accepted rules.
There is no rounding selector or implied current balance.

**Given** the remaining sections,
**When** I configure the policy,
**Then** they cover paid/unpaid classification, permitted units, duration limits,
notice/backdating/booking rules, balance-shortfall behavior, eligibility,
cancellation/amendment rules, approval requirements, documents and privacy,
**And** exact field ownership and supported combinations follow the authoritative contracts.

**Given** approval configuration,
**When** I choose one or two steps,
**Then** at least one approval remains required; two steps require an explicitly selected
eligible final approver,
**And** no CEO is preselected and selecting an approver grants no permissions. Workflow
execution remains E5's responsibility.

**Given** valid completed input,
**When** I select Review changes,
**Then** the review shows the proposed rules and effective date, with Back to editing
and Publish policy version,
**And** reviewing publishes nothing. Missing or inconsistent required settings prevent publication.

**Given** a reviewed configuration and current authority,
**When** I confirm publication,
**Then** the server atomically records the initial immutable policy version, attribution
and required change evidence,
**And** duplicate retries publish only once. Concurrent publication or changed reviewed
inputs require safe conflict handling.

**Given** future-dated publication,
**When** publication succeeds,
**Then** confirmation says Policy scheduled for [date] and the summary labels it Scheduled,
**And** it does not imply a currently effective policy.

**Given** validation, authorization or transport failure,
**When** publication cannot be confirmed,
**Then** input remains available for correction or recovery; an uncertain outcome is
resolved before another attempt,
**And** keyboard/mobile operation follows approved UX.

**Traceability / planned verification:** Features §4/7/10; BIZ-06/19/20 (partial coverage);
applicable CALC configuration and FLOW-01/03/07/20 inputs; Leave ADR-0002/0086/0090,
0050/0036, 0085/0089, 0098–0105, 0124 and applicable approval decisions with supersessions;
approved Leave EXPERIENCE policy editor/review and platform saving/recovery contracts.
Configuration tests prove accepted conditional combinations and defaults, including zero
notice, twelve-month horizon and monthly partial-employment adjustment, without executing
future calculation/submission/approval behavior. Document threshold distinguishes above
two days from exactly two; examples are illustrative, not statutory defaults. Pair real
API/database permission, scoped publication, immutable version, concurrent first-publication,
revision/operation and lost-response tests with browser edit/review/back/publish, future
status, validation/error, mobile/keyboard and input-preservation checks. Final source-to-test
mapping, exact paths/commands and sizing remain pending; no runtime tests executed.

**Pre-story inputs / sizing:** Bind the complete field schema, valid combinations,
data ownership, effective-date interpretation, scoped approver lookup, policy/choice
metadata interaction, concurrency and publication API/error/operation contracts. Initial
unused-state validation must exclude existing employee entitlement effects; do not hide
required notification, recalculation or affected-request handling here. Group 5 precedes
any mutation requiring notification. Full policy validation, interpretation and source
examples remain authority; this scope does not replace the remaining calculation contracts.
If final sizing requires splitting the editor/publication work, reconcile independently
working dependencies collaboratively before implementation; no future-story prerequisite
or unfinished policy exposed as active. All readiness gates remain open.

Contract terminology clarified with the user — 2026-10-12: contracts are written technical
agreements about behavior and information exchanged by components, not legal agreements.
Field ownership means Leave owns policy settings while shared employee facts retain their
service owner; supported combinations mean conditional/validation rules. Publication
contracts bind permission, validation, immutable save/effective date, attribution,
duplicate-safe retry and changed-review handling. The user preferred retaining the term;
no settled business decision reopened.

**Impacts:** Scaffold: reuse/prove generic version publication, review/revision/outcome
and attribution mechanisms with thin schema-validated inputs and reference tests where
applicable; no shared policy/calculation engine. Shared UI: reuse dedicated-form sections,
conditional fields, review, navigation and recovery; promote proven domain-neutral
patterns in the consuming delivery item. Agent context: existing instructions suffice.
Documentation: policy/publication contracts, source/test mappings, epics/tracker checkpoint.
ADR: accepted decisions suffice; no amendment. No implementation or readiness authorization.

### Story 3.3-A: Review and publish an initial policy through the API


**Child scope approved — 2026-10-15; not implementation-ready.** Parent: Story 3.3.
Owner: Leave initial-policy validation/review/publication API and persistence. Delivery
position: after 3.2, before 3.3-B and 3.4; this appendix position is not execution order.
Consumes E1/E2 current authority, owned-write, version, operation/recovery foundations.
Initial-policy fixtures do not depend on later assignment/calculation/request writers.

As an authorized Leave Manager,
I want policy configuration validated and published through a protected API,
So that only complete, reviewed rules become effective.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a leave type eligible for initial policy setup,
**When** configuration is validated,
**Then** the API checks supported fields, required values and permitted combinations,
including automatic, manual-only and untracked policies.

**Given** incomplete or incompatible configuration,
**When** validation runs,
**Then** stable field-specific errors identify what needs correction,
**And** nothing is published.

**Given** valid configuration,
**When** review is requested,
**Then** the API returns proposed settings, applicable defaults and effective-date
information without creating business effects.

**Given** current permission and unchanged consequential review inputs,
**When** publication is confirmed,
**Then** the immutable policy version, attribution and required change evidence commit
atomically.

**Given** concurrent publication, changed reviewed inputs or a lost response,
**When** confirmation or recovery occurs,
**Then** stale confirmation is rejected where necessary,
**And** retries cannot publish duplicate versions.

**Given** successful publication,
**When** the policy is read,
**Then** current or scheduled status and effective dates are represented accurately,
**And** publication creates no employee assignment or access grant.

**Given** initial policy settings,
**When** the supported field matrix is validated,
**Then** name/code/description/color/icon and active dates, paid/unpaid classification, allowed full/half/hour units, automatic daily/upfront/monthly versus manual-only versus untracked category, allowance, proration, accumulation cap, carry-over/expiry, minimum/maximum duration, notice/backdate/advance horizon, projected funding/shortfall, document condition/threshold, privacy and supported one-/two-step approval settings each have typed validated representation under the accepted source rules; no unknown generic rule expression is accepted.

**Given** new automatic-entitlement configuration without an explicit user choice,
**When** defaults are proposed for review,
**Then** upfront availability and calendar-day adjustment for time employed are selected under ADR-0127, notice defaults to zero and the request horizon to twelve months; explicit existing selections are retained and the review still creates no assignment or grant.

**Given** conditional policy settings,
**When** configuration is validated,
**Then** limited carry-over requires its amount, enabled carry-over binds expiry/repetition, capped accumulation requires its amount, two steps require the configured eligible final position and threshold-based documents require their threshold; hidden incompatible values cannot silently supply runtime authority.

**Given** a document threshold, duration bounds or request-horizon boundary,
**When** the configured rule is evaluated through the authoritative projection,
**Then** exactly two days does not exceed a longer-than-two-days document threshold while three does, minimum/maximum limits use authoritative duration and every requested date respects the advance horizon; no jurisdictional threshold is invented.

**Traceability / planned verification:** Parent 3.3 backend acceptance and source links:
Features §4/7/10; BIZ-06/19/20 configuration; FLOW-01/03/07/20 inputs; applicable accepted
policy/default/version/conditional-field decisions, including ADR-0127/0133–0135/0140.
This child supplies 3.40's explicit untracked backend configuration behavior when sized
into delivery; do not implement or count it twice. Real API/database tests prove complete
field validation, stable typed errors, no review effects, eligible unused-state guard,
current scoped authority, immutable version/evidence atomicity/rollback, concurrency,
changed-input review and lost-response deduplication. Read tests prove current/scheduled
dates and no assignment/grant side effects. No runtime tests executed; exact paths/
commands and atomic field-to-test mapping remain pre-story inputs.

**Pre-story inputs / sizing:** Bind full field/combination schema, unused/in-use history,
approver lookup/configuration contracts, effective-date/read DTOs, review evidence,
operation/revision guards and owner write permissions. Later adopted rules do not create
a dependency on their later app writers: prove this bounded initial configuration with
declared owner fixtures. No partial invalid policy activation, extra admin draft system,
approval execution, entitlement assignment or hidden notification producer. Final agent
sizing/coverage/readiness remain open.

**Impacts:** Scaffold: prove/promote owned validation/review/version/operation/error/
attribution/client patterns and actual tests; Leave owns policy fields and rules. Shared
UI: no editor in this child; generated typed errors/read contracts support 3.3-B. Agent
context: existing instructions suffice. Documentation: API/field/publication/test contracts,
parent-child acceptance mapping and tracker/handoff. ADR: accepted decisions suffice.
No implementation/readiness permission.

As an authorized Leave Manager,
I want a clear policy editor with review before publication,
So that I can configure complete rules and confirm them deliberately.

**Then** the dedicated page provides four directly accessible sections: Entitlement,
Request rules, Approval, and Documents & privacy.

**Given** my configuration choices,
**When** I edit settings,
**Then** applicable fields and plain-language explanations appear, including automatic,
manual-only and No balance tracking options,
**And** approved defaults remain editable; incompatible hidden values cannot be published.

**Given** incomplete or invalid input,
**When** validation returns errors,
**Then** they appear beside relevant fields, entered values remain available and I can
navigate to each issue.

**Given** valid input,
**When** I select Review changes,

outcome recovery. Verify keyboard/mobile/focus and changed-form exit, with no extra admin
draft or premature effects. Exact source/test paths/commands remain pre-story inputs;
no runtime tests executed.

**Pre-story inputs / sizing:** Bind generated API/error/review types and field matrix,

Agent context: existing instructions suffice. Documentation: field/UI/API/test contracts,
parent-child mapping and tracker/handoff. ADR: accepted decisions suffice. No code or
implementation/readiness permission.

### Story 3.40: Configure a policy with no balance tracking

**Consolidated coverage record — 2026-10-16:** Scope remains approved; no separate delivery
item. Allocate initial field/editor/review/publication criteria to 3.3-A/B, policy-summary
criterion to 3.2 and used-category guards to 3.34-A/B as mapped above. Preserve every
criterion and test/source link; this prevents duplicate implementation, not scope removal.

**Scope approved — 2026-10-15; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave policy
configuration/publication API, web editor and policy summaries. Extends prior configuration,
version/review and read foundations under ADR-0135; independent of later untracked
calculation/employee-preview consumers, which must prove their actual integration before
activation. No submission or approval workflow implemented in this scope.

As a Leave Manager with policy-management permission,
I want to configure a policy without an entitlement balance,
So that leave can be requested and approved without maintaining an allowance.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** initial policy configuration,
**When** I choose how entitlement is managed,
**Then** No balance tracking is available separately from automatic entitlement and
manual-only grants.

**Given** No balance tracking is selected,
**When** I configure the policy,
**Then** irrelevant allowance, earning, balance-cap, carry-over, entitlement-expiry and
balance-shortfall controls are hidden,
**And** the backend rejects incompatible settings rather than relying on hidden controls.

**Given** an untracked policy,
**When** I configure its remaining rules,
**Then** paid/unpaid classification, permitted units, request restrictions, documents,
privacy and approval requirements remain applicable.

**Given** valid configuration,
**When** I review and publish it,
**Then** the summary clearly says No balance tracking and explains that request rules
and approval still apply,
**And** existing versioning, authorization, confirmation and duplicate-prevention
safeguards remain binding.

**Given** a published untracked policy,
**When** an authorized user views its summary,
**Then** it identifies leave as Not balance-limited,
**And** it displays neither zero entitlement nor an invented unlimited balance.

**Given** a policy already in use,
**When** someone attempts to change between tracked and untracked,
**Then** the backend rejects the unsupported conversion,
**And** the editor explains the restriction.

**Traceability / planned verification:** Features §4/6 and applicable request/approval
configuration; BIZ-05/06/09/19/20; Leave ADR-0002/0090/0124/0135 and policy editor/summary
UX. Real API/database/browser tests prove distinct categories, conditional controls and
server validation of incompatible fields, independent paid/unpaid/request/approval rules,
explicit review/publication, immutable scoped versions/evidence, summary wording, direct
conversion denial and concurrency/current authority/retry protections. Exercise initial
category changes before publication without leaking hidden incompatible values. No
runtime tests executed; exact source/test paths and commands remain pre-story inputs.

**Pre-story inputs / sizing:** Bind policy schema/conditional field matrix, representation
of inapplicable settings, initial unused-state/in-use guards and all writer/replacement
paths. Retain explicit publication and no persisted administrative draft requirement.
Later consumers require explicit supported untracked semantics before activation; policy
configuration alone is not proof of request correctness. Exact contracts, agent sizing,
coverage and all readiness gates remain open.

**Impacts:** Scaffold: prove/promote conditional typed configuration/review/version/error
patterns with consuming tests; Leave owns entitlement applicability. Shared UI: reuse
four-section editor and readable policy summary with No balance tracking/Not balance-limited
wording; no generic policy engine. Agent context: existing instructions suffice.
Documentation: policy field/combination/publication/test contracts and tracker/handoff.
ADR: accepted ADR-0135 suffices. No implementation/readiness permission.

### Story 3.4: Review starter examples before activating a policy

**Scope approved by the user, 2026-10-12, with the presentation/confirmation refinements
above; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave. Consumes Stories 3.1–3.3, E1 scoped
type identities and E2 saved work-profile/calendar facts. Uses the existing editor and
publication review, without a separate organization sign-off process.

As a Leave Manager configuring an organization,
I want editable starter examples that require review before activation,
So that setup is quicker while the organization explicitly confirms its own rules.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** initial policy setup,
**When** I choose a starter example for Annual, Sick or Family Responsibility Leave,
**Then** it prefills the existing policy editor without publishing anything,
**And** it reuses the organization's type identities rather than creating duplicates.

**Given** example settings,
**When** I review them,
**Then** they are clearly labelled Starter example and remain editable,
**And** example content does not claim universal legal/country allowances. No separate
legal warning, explanatory panel or repeated disclaimer is required in the interface.

**Given** the starter approval configuration,
**When** it is loaded,
**Then** it uses one supervisor step, self-approval off, temporary cover supported,
three-day reminders and seven-day escalation,
**And** a second step and directional absence fallback remain optional and off initially.
Actual workflow execution, appointments and due work belong to E5.

**Given** a proposed starter policy,
**When** activation is reviewed,
**Then** the Leave Manager with current policy-management permission confirms they have
reviewed entitlement, work schedules, holiday calendars and organization-specific rules
during the existing publication review,
**And** missing required configuration is explained without a false Ready result.
No separate client approval role or sign-off workflow is introduced.

**Given** confirmed valid settings,
**When** I publish,
**Then** Story 3.3's permission, versioning, effective-date and retry protections apply,
**And** no employment, employee assignment or application grant is created automatically.

**Traceability / planned verification:** Features §4/10; BIZ-06/19; FLOW-03;
approved Leave EXPERIENCE starter-policy/editor and platform explicit-save/review UX.
Verify prefill, unchanged stable type identities, approved defaults versus editable
choices, explicit authorized confirmation, required-setting failures and duplicate-safe
publication through the actual editor/API. Preserve E1's unconfigured draft-choice
behavior and group 5's notification-before-consuming-mutation boundary.
No runtime tests executed; final source/test paths/commands remain pending.

**Pre-story inputs / sizing:** Bind reviewed example contents and owning provisioning,
the confirmation/evidence shape within the existing publication contract, and required
configuration predicates using actual E2 facts. No inferred statutory allowance, new
policy assignment default, approval execution, stored manual readiness flag or dependency
on group 8's later setup UI. This story proves its own required checks. Publication is
initial unused-policy setup under Story 3.3; notified existing-entitlement changes remain
later consumers. Exact technical/test contracts and final agent sizing/readiness remain open.

**Impacts:** Scaffold: reuse existing configuration/example and version/review patterns;
keep Leave example content out of generic generation. Shared UI: reuse editor/review and
concise example labels; no new warning/sign-off component. Agent context: existing
instructions suffice. Documentation: maintained starter examples, publication/test
mapping and epics/tracker/handoff checkpoint. ADR: accepted decisions suffice; no amendment.

### Story 3.5: Explain which policy applies to an employee

**Scope approved by the user, 2026-10-12, with the ambiguity/unavailability refinement
below; not implementation-ready.** Owner: Leave, consuming authorized shared employment
facts over HTTP. Consumes initial policy/read foundations and E2 employee facts; group 2
applicability read only, not entitlement override, adjustment or submission execution.

As a Leave Manager with current permission to view an employee's Leave settings,
I want to check which policy applies for a selected leave type and date,
So that I can understand eligibility and identify configuration gaps.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** an authorized employee, leave type and selected date,
**When** I check applicability,
**Then** the backend identifies the applicable policy version and evaluates its configured
eligibility rules,
**And** the result names the policy and explains the relevant conditions in plain language.

**Given** eligibility depends on employment type, location, tenure or assignment,
**When** those conditions are evaluated,
**Then** the check uses the applicable facts for that date from their owning services
or Leave settings,
**And** it does not duplicate shared employment information or infer eligibility from
application roles.

**Given** no applicable policy or unmet eligibility conditions,
**When** the check completes,
**Then** it explains the missing configuration or unmet condition,
**And** it distinguishes that result from a failed check.

**Given** a future policy version,
**When** I select dates before and after its effective boundary,
**Then** each check uses the version applicable to that date rather than today's policy.

**Given** required employment or policy information cannot be retrieved,
**When** applicability is checked,
**Then** show Couldn't check with Retry,
**And** do not treat the failure as employee ineligibility.

**Given** conflicting policy applicability rules,
**When** they are saved,
**Then** reject them with an explanation of what needs correcting,
**And** enforce this in the owning write path, including concurrent saves, rather than
accepting ambiguity and expecting employees to resolve it. The matching contract defines
what constitutes conflict; relevant existing policy writers integrate/prove this safeguard
in the same delivery item. No new assignment writer depends on a future story here.

**Given** an applicability check,
**When** the result is displayed,
**Then** it changes no employee settings, grants, balances or reservations,
**And** draft preservation remains available under its existing protections.

**Given** current or future explicit employee-policy assignments and employee-filter facts,
**When** applicability is read or relevant published configuration is validated,
**Then** MVP eligibility uses the explicitly confirmed assignment and applicable policy version together with ordinary employment/date rules; changing employment type, location, tenure, filters or the employee list cannot create, end or replace assignment,
**And** generalized eligibility/conflicting-rule wording above does not introduce automatic eligibility expressions or a rule engine under ADR-0126. Earlier existing writers reject unsupported rule settings; the actual 3.28/3.36 assignment writers enforce concurrent nonconflicting coverage when those writers are delivered.

**Traceability / planned verification:** Features §4, BIZ-06/07 (partial coverage),
Leave policy/versioning decisions and platform shared-employment ownership; approved
employee-setting/access/error UX. Verify date-version matching, accepted eligibility
combinations, missing versus unavailable facts, explained unmet conditions, protected
employee scope, organization isolation and delayed response context. Pair conflict-save
validation with real database/API concurrent-writer evidence; browser explanations alone
cannot establish matching integrity. Applicable configuration writers must participate.
No runtime tests executed; final source/test paths/commands remain pending.

**Pre-story inputs / sizing:** Settle exact matching/precedence, employment-type ownership,
tenure treatment across employment periods and date interpretation. These remain explicit
open inputs; no guessed universal tenure restart, inferred policy assignment/role grant,
cross-owner table access or silent new business rule. Define and test the write safeguards
alongside the resolver, within completed dependencies; split if final sizing requires it.
Unavailable dependency data is not invalid configuration. Accepted refinement prevents
normal ambiguous saves instead of introducing routine employee ambiguity handling.
Final agent sizing and readiness remain open.

**Impacts:** Scaffold: prove/reuse generic current authorized service inputs, safe
error/context and scoped constraint patterns, not a shared eligibility engine. Shared UI:
reuse result/loading/retry controls and scoped employee/type/date selection; Leave owns
matching and explanations. Agent context: existing instructions suffice. Documentation:
matching/ownership contracts, source/test mapping and epics/tracker/handoff checkpoint.
ADR: existing accepted decisions remain authority; raise a new business outcome for
discussion if resolution requires one. No implementation or readiness authorization.

### Explicit policy assignment decision — accepted 2026-10-12

User approved filters plus explicit employee policy assignment for MVP, deferring
automatic eligibility rules. [ADR-0126](../../apps/leave/docs/architecture/decisions/0126-explicit-policy-assignment-with-employee-filters.md)
and features §4 are authoritative. Filter changes, new employees and changed employment
facts do not dynamically add/remove assignments. Managers maintain the exact reviewed
set; backend consequential checks enforce applicable assignment alongside existing rules.
No access grant, recurring override, balance reset or weakened draft preservation.

This later decision refines agreed Story 3.3's eligibility configuration and Story 3.5's

employment-type/location/tenure matching. Conflict-save rejection and Couldn't check /
Retry for outages remain agreed. Exact assignment/version/date/conflict and supported
filter-fact contracts stay open; there is no new universal tenure rule or missing-fact
inference. Preserve historical evidence, actual effect review and required notifications.
Finalize coherent story acceptance/test mapping before readiness; historical proposals
above do not override this accepted amendment.

Impacts: authority/spec/spine/UX/tracker/handoff updated; new additive Leave ADR, accepted
predecessors unchanged. Reuse proven generic filters/selection/review/recovery in UI and

agent-context rule. Assignment writers needing calculation/notification effects follow
